steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Configure CORS** in *CORS: what it is and what it isn't*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A team says: "Our API is safe from scrapers because CORS only allows `https://app.example`." Why is that wrong?
options: CORS is enforced by browsers; a script using curl or HttpClient ignores it entirely
CORS headers can be forged by the browser
CORS only applies to GET requests
It is right: CORS blocks all other clients
